subject: Post‑call: model recommendations + prompt / redaction capture (EdgeCorp)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model recommendations + prompt / redaction capture (EdgeCorp)

Hi Ava — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our discovery:

Summary of needs (from our notes):
- Primary workload: customer support triage + short-summarization + policy classification (~6–12 tokens/sec target).
- Quality constraints: high precision on policy matches, low hallucination tolerance for regulatory responses.
- Data residency: US-only logs; need audit trail and retention options.
- Edge cases: long multi-turn threads with embedded PII, legal citations, and code snippets.

Initial model fit suggestions (based on the call):
- Redwood-7B-v2 (quantized): good cost/latency balance for classification and summary tasks.
- RedOpt-13B-Q4: stronger on instruction-following and few-shot extraction; recommended for fallback for complex cases.
- If ultra low-latency golden-path required, we can test a trimmed Redwood-3B variant with tighter chunking.

Benchmarks and artifacts I attached: redwood_benchmarks_q3_2026.pdf — contains token-level latency and quality-tradeoff curves for the above models measured on representative support threads.

Action items / asks we need from EdgeCorp to proceed with a short eval: 
1) Prompt set: can you share ~30 representative prompts (real or synthetic) covering the happy paths + 10–15 edge cases (especially ones with PII and mixed content)? Please include expected labels/outputs if available.
2) Redaction guidance: please upload your redaction policy or call out fields you consider sensitive (PII, PHI, legal identifiers). We can map that to automatic redaction and filtering rules.
3) Success metric: confirm the primary metric (e.g., classification precision @0.8 threshold, F1 for extraction, or human approval rate).
4) Preference on hosted vs private test run (we can run a blinded bench on hosted infra or do a VPC-provisioned evaluation).

Proposed next steps: you share prompt files and redaction doc into the Drive folder I created; we’ll run a 48h bench and share a short quality/latency report and a recommended model+quantization profile. If that looks good, we’ll scope a pilot (2–4 week) with canary routing and regression monitoring.

Availability: I’m booking a 30min bench-readout slot for Fri 9/17 10:00–10:30 PT; does that work?

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: model recommendations + prompt / redaction capture (EdgeCorp)

Diego — great recap, thanks. Confirming availability for Fri 9/17 10:00 PT. A few notes and I attached our redaction guidance: edgecorp-redaction-guidelines.pdf.

On the asks:
- Prompt set: attaching three representative examples below (we'll upload the full set to the Drive link you shared as soon as legal signs off):
  1) "Customer: I was charged twice for the same invoice. Please refund." (expected: route: billing_refund; extract: invoice_number if present)
  2) "Customer: My account was locked, it says breach detected. What do I do?" (expected: route: security_escalation; templated response + triage steps)
  3) "Customer: Here is my SSN 123-45-6789 — I need to update my profile." (expected: redact SSN, route: sensitive_handling)
- Edge cases to include: long email threads with inline attachments, legal citation requests, code block in technical support.
- Success metric: our internal bar is 90% precision on routing for Tier-1 cases; 85% for Tier-2 extraction tasks.

We prefer a hosted blind bench first (faster) but need logs redacted per our policy — we can provide a scrub script if needed.

Thanks, will upload the ~40-prompt set by EOD Thu and share a short doc on redaction mapping.

— Ava
Ava Collins
Head of Product, EdgeCorp
Ava.Collins@edgecorp.com
Attachments: edgecorp-redaction-guidelines.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: model recommendations + prompt / redaction capture (EdgeCorp)

Looping in some technical context from our eval team. A few notes we should surface to EdgeCorp in the bench: 

- Quantization profile: for Redwood-7B-v2 we recommend int4-cheap for most classification tasks; increases throughput ~2.4x with minimal precision drop on our internal datasets. We should show both int4 and int8 curves in the bench.
- Regression guardrails: we'll include a small seeded prompt set (10 golden prompts) to verify no quality regressions across rollouts; propose we lock those as a pass/fail gating metric.
- Privacy: we'll run redaction heuristics pre-send and include a redaction report (samples removed / token counts).
- Runbook: plan to expose a temporary readonly S3 bucket for results; we can also publish an anonymized artifact into the Drive folder.

Rishi — can you pre-provision a hosted bench job and tag it EDGE-4521? Estimate: 48h run (5000 sample tokens / prompt set variations). I'll prepare the Jupyter notebook that generates the QC charts.

Thanks, Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
